title: Proactive kernel coalescer and phased rollout for FlashAttention v2/v3 regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are seeing intermittent latency spikes and workspace OOMs in production after enabling several FlashAttention v3 execution paths across heterogeneous GPU fleets. Root cause analysis points to frequent kernel oscillation and small-shape memory fragmentation when multiple concurrent prefill/decode shapes are scheduled, which increases decode tail latency and occasionally causes v3 kernels to fail and fallback mid-request.

Goal:
Build a proactive 'kernel coalescer' in the serving runtime that groups similar attention requests (shape, precision, layout, quantization profile) before kernel selection to reduce oscillation and workspace churn. Pair the coalescer with a phased, telemetry-driven rollout for v3 variants that includes shape-aware canaries, gradual ramping, and automated rollback triggers based on SLO regressions. The combined approach should reduce tail latency, lower kernel switch frequency, and eliminate regression-induced errors.

Scope and deliverables:
- Coalescer runtime component: single-thread safe grouping layer that collects small windows of incoming attention requests and emits coalesced scheduling hints to the kernel selector. Configurable time budget (ms), shape similarity thresholds, and max coalesced batch size.
- Kernel selector integration: allow selector to prefer stable kernel choices for coalesced groups and attach a group id to telemetry for tracing.
- Canary plan: shape-aware canaries (short, mid, long sequence lengths; 1/2/4k tokens; quantized/FP16 mixes). Canary traffic routing and scoring in Console.
- Rollout automation: ramp percentages, SLO gates (p95 decode, p99 tail, error-rate, OOM count), and automated rollback policy.
- Tests and validation: microbenchmarks, replay tests with recorded traffic shapes, heavy-priming stress tests to surface workspace contention, and synthetic multi-tenant experiments.
- Observability: new telemetry fields (coalesced_group, kernel_choice_reason, kernel_switch_count) and dashboards for heatmaps and correlation with OOMs/latency.

Success metrics:
- Reduce kernel_switch_count per-request by >= 65% for mixed-shape workloads in canary region.
- Reduce p99 decode latency by >= 20% for affected workloads.
- Eliminate regression OOMs in canary window and reduce production OOM alerts to baseline.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design & API (week 1): define coalescer contract with kernel selector, group metadata, and config knobs (time_budget_ms, similarity_threshold, max_group_size, min_hold_count). Doc: confluence/serving/kernel-coalescer-design.
2) Prototype (week 2): lightweight in-thread coalescer with unit tests and sim harness for shape distributions. Early perf metrics and safety fences.
3) Selector integration (week 3): emit kernel hints, attach group id to request context, allow selector to consider group statistics before switching kernels.
4) Telemetry & dashboards (week 3): add coalesced_group, kernel_choice_reason, kernel_switch_count to traces and metrics pipeline. Dashboard for canary monitoring.
5) Canary (week 4): run 2% productionish traffic in canary region with shape-sampled traffic. Monitor SLOs for 48h. If stable, increase to 10% then 25% with staged checks.
6) Rollout (week 5): gradual ramp to full region with roll-forward and rollback automation.

Safety and rollback:
- Hard limits: if kernel_switch_count or p99 decode latency increases >10% above baseline during any ramp step, immediately cut canary back and disable v3 kernels for affected shapes.
- Fallback policy: keep v2/legacy kernels available as a fallback; coalescer must mark group-level fallback to avoid oscillation on retries.
- Circuit breaker: global disable toggle and per-shape disable lists.
comments: 2025-02-05 — Kickoff: design doc draft uploaded to confluence (confluence.redwood.com/display/RUN/Kernel+Coalescer+Design). Agree to conservative default time_budget_ms=3ms and max_group_size=8 to avoid decode latency bleed. — Aisha

2025-02-11 — Prototype complete: in-thread coalescer prototype reduced simulated kernel switch events by 58% on recorded chat workload (mixed 512/1024/2048 shapes). Memory overhead negligible in microbench. Posting PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/2387 — Marco

2025-02-18 — Selector integration review: PM requested adding kernel_choice_reason enum to make rollout decisions auditable. Added test harness to assert group-level fallback path correctness when a kernel fails mid-request. PR updated to 2395. — Marco

2025-02-23 — Canary prep: created dashboard 'Coalescer / Kernel Rollout (canary)' with heatmaps for kernel_switch_count and OOM event spikes. Alert rule: if OOMs > 3 in 10m in canary, auto-rollback. — SRE (Daniel)

2025-02-25 — Early canary (2%): no OOMs observed, p95 improved 12%, p99 unchanged. Noted small increase in latency for 1-of-8 micro-batched groups; reducing time_budget_ms to 2ms helped. Incrementing to 10% tomorrow. — Marco

2025-03-01 — 10% canary: kernel_switch_count down 71%, p99 decode improved 18% for chat workloads, but observed a single v3 kernel failure tied to an uncommon quantized layout (edge case). Added shape to per-shape disable list and created follow-up ENG-613102 to expand layout matrix tests. — Aisha

2025-03-02 — Technical review: design approved by runtime leads. Next steps: broader replay testing in perf lab, finalize rollout automation runbook, and handoff to SRE for long-running monitoring. — Priya (engineering lead)
notes: Follow-up tickets: expand layout fuzz tests (ENG-613102), integrate coalescer with autoscaler feedback loop (ENG-614000). Consider exploring coalescer + KV-cache prefetch hints in a separate spike.
